crisisTimeline.title: Trump calls off planned Tuesday Iran strikes — Gulf Arab leaders broker talks; Pentagon on standby
crisisTimeline.description: Trump called off attacks on Iran scheduled for Tuesday May 19 at the request of Gulf Arab allies — Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE. Leaders told Trump that 'serious negotiations are underway with Iran that will result in a deal acceptable to the US.' Trump instructed the Pentagon to be 'prepared to go forward with a full, large scale assault of Iran, on a moment's notice, in the event that an acceptable Deal is not reached.' Earlier in the session Trump warned 'the clock is ticking' for Iran, driving early oil gains. Despite the calloff, oil prices held all gains: Brent +2% to $112.10 settle, WTI +3% to $108.66. IEA May 2026 Oil Market Report (published May 13) projected Q2 global inventory draws of 8.5 mb/d — steepest in May-June — and warned 'Rapidly shrinking buffers amid continued disruptions may herald future price spikes ahead.' ~164 mb of the 400 mb IEA emergency release already drawn. Crisis Day 80.

crisisTimeline.title: US thwarts attacks on 3 Navy ships in Strait + retaliates against Iranian facilities
crisisTimeline.description: First direct US Navy / Iranian Navy fire exchange of the crisis. US said it thwarted Iranian attacks on three Navy ships transiting the Strait, then retaliated against Iranian military facilities. UAE simultaneously intercepted two ballistic missiles and three drones launched by Iran the same day — three wounded. Brent closes the week at $111.04, +8.1% week. Crisis enters Day 77.

crisisTimeline.title: Trump-Xi Beijing summit: both agree Strait 'must remain open'; China to work behind scenes on Iran
crisisTimeline.description: Trump and Xi Jinping, meeting at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, jointly published nine commitments including: Strait of Hormuz 'must remain open', Iran 'can never have nuclear weapons'. Xi expressed opposition to any toll or militarization of the Strait, and interest in purchasing more US oil to reduce China's Hormuz dependence. Treasury Secretary Bessent (CNBC): China will 'work behind the scenes to the extent anyone has any say over the Iranian leadership.' China cited as having the greatest interest in reopening — nearly all Iranian crude exports flow to China. Complication: a vessel was seized near the Strait by 'unauthorized personnel' and taken toward Iran during the summit. Saudi June OSP for Asia cut to +$15.50/bbl above Oman/Dubai (from record +$19.50 May). Brent fell from $111 to ~$106 on the news; WTI held above $101. Dubai inverted to $5 discount vs Brent — first since crisis onset.

crisisTimeline.title: EIA: record 8.6 Mb single-week SPR withdrawal — biggest ever
crisisTimeline.description: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report (week ending May 8): SPR drew a record 8.6 Mb, beating the prior all-time weekly high of 8.4 Mb set in September 2022. SPR now stands at 384.1 Mb — lowest since October 2024. Commercial crude stocks −4.3 Mb. Refineries ran 16.4 Mbpd at 91.7% capacity utilization (+369 kbpd WoW). The US is bleeding from every barrel source simultaneously to keep products flowing.

crisisTimeline.title: Operation Freedom suspended after 1-ship-in-24h transit print + 24 Mbbl API draw
crisisTimeline.description: Trump abruptly suspended Operation Freedom — the latest attempt to reopen Strait traffic — after market close on May 6. Catalyst: JaguarAnalytics daily transit tracker showed just 1 ship crossing the Strait in the prior 24 hours, and API printed a ~24 Mbbl total-products inventory draw for the week. MacroEdge estimates 13.5–14 Mbpd remaining offline (vs HFI's 11.5) and expects strait normalization no earlier than late summer / fall, citing the IRGC's strategic interest in maintaining long-term Strait control as a revenue stream.

Cumulative ~330 Mbbl drawn over Mar+Apr. Dec '26 Brent sub-$80 vs front $110 implies rapid normalization the supply math doesn't support. IEA's 120-day SPR window exhausts ~Jul 9.

recoveryClock.keyInsight: Asia passed the point of no return by the second week of the closure. Even if the strait reopens tomorrow, 4-5 months before any sense of normalcy returns. HALO — Hard Assets, Local Operations — is the post-Hormuz regime. — HFI Research (May 19, 2026) flags the point of no return: ballast tankers redirected to US drainage make Persian Gulf restart impossible before August, regardless of when the strait reopens. HFI thesis: until refining margins peak and roll over, the inventory-vs-prompt-price inverse correlation argues current oil is mispriced low.
refiningMargins.hfiThesis: If you want to know when it's time to get bearish oil, just watch refining margins. In COVID, floating storage, tanker rates, contango, and refining margins all peaked first. Then margins went negative. When they rebounded, crude rallied. This time around, a similar playbook will happen but in reverse — refining margins will be the key indicator for when the global economy cannot handle higher prices any longer.

tankerEconomics.title: Tanker Day Rates
tankerEconomics.insight: VLCC TD3 at 3.2× baseline. Freight rates historically lead spot Brent by 1–3 trading days — when arbitrage opens, freight prices in first. The Worldscale jump from WS50 to WS135 reflects both the war-risk premium and the cape-of-good-hope rerouting cost; both ease only after Hormuz transit normalizes.
tankerEconomics.source: Baltic Exchange BDTI · Clarksons · Argus Freight
tankerEconomics.methodology: VLCC TD3 is the canonical 270,000 dwt MEG→China VLCC route published daily by the Baltic Exchange (BDTI sub-index). Worldscale (WS) is the freight-pricing convention: WS100 = the published flat rate for a given route; a fixture done at WS135 pays 135% of that reference. Suezmax (MEG→Europe) and Aframax (Mediterranean) supply complementary route reads. Day-rate equivalents use Clarksons time-charter-equivalent (TCE) conversions; intraday quotes via Argus Freight.

volSkew.title: Vol Skew · Options Market Expectations
volSkew.insight: Risk reversal at +3 vol pts with front ATM IV at 2.2× baseline = the options market is committing to a bullish directional view with material conviction. Term structure backwards (52% / 45% / 38%) — near-term stress dominates; calls are bid both absolutely (call skew +8 vol pts) and relatively (RR +3). When risk reversal stays positive while ATM IV rises, that is the cleanest options-market read on directional expectations: dealers are willing to pay up for upside protection.
volSkew.source: CBOE OVX · ICE Brent options surface · Bloomberg consensus
volSkew.methodology: Risk reversal = 25-delta call IV minus 25-delta put IV. Positive = call options bid relative to puts (bullish positioning by options market). ATM IV tells you implied daily move size; term structure backwardation (front > 3M > 6M) indicates near-term stress.

physicalMarketNotes.quote: Brent options have repriced the front-end like a war. ATM IV at 52% vs 24% in January — that is more than a doubling in the implied daily move. Risk reversal has stayed bid through the entire reload of the curve, which tells you dealers can't find natural sellers of upside. Until backwardation in vol flattens, every dip is a gift to systematic long-vol books.

criticalPath.title: HFI Critical Path — When the Thesis Plays Out
criticalPath.subtitle: Death by a thousand headlines is delaying demand destruction. Two specific dated milestones determine when oil math forces price discovery.
criticalPath.framing: Jawbones are buying time, not changing fundamentals. The oil math at 4× historical supply shock scale doesn't care about Truth Social. Either US/Iran re-escalates (traders scramble for August barrels) or we go straight to operational minimums. Pick your poison.

milestones.label: US crude exports priced out
milestones.description: Marginal barrel cushion exhausted. US has offset 25% of global crude export decline via record 5,750 kbbl/d exports. When that's priced out, the rest of the world competes for the 1–2 mb/d gap.

milestones.label: US commercial crude → operational minimum
milestones.description: US commercial storage reaches the JH MOI floor (~290 mb). US is the LAST place to draw (structural: shale ultra-light sweet vs heavy/medium sour refinery needs). When US can't supply the gap, sidelined buyers are forced into desperate bidding. Phase 3.
